Workflow comparison

CardScanFox vs Ludex: scan to collection or scan to listing?

CardScanFox is an option for reviewing card matches and tracking confirmed holdings. Ludex documents a scan-to-eBay-listing workflow. Choose by the task after scanning; this comparison does not establish an accuracy or speed winner.

CardScanFox is available on iPhone and Android. Both stores currently list it as Card AI: TCG Card Scanner.

DownloadApp Store DownloadGoogle Play

How should I choose between CardScanFox and Ludex?

  1. Decide whether you need collection records or an eBay listing workflow. Review the dated official sources linked below for the other product.
  2. Check that your game and exact printing are available. Try a small group of known cards, including any parallel or existing slab you need to record.
  3. In CardScanFox, confirm the suggested printing, finish and language. Enter raw condition or an existing slab grade before saving the holding.
  4. Check the currency, date and meaning of each available price. Do not compare a reference price, a sold transaction and a listing ask as the same measure.

A wrong match needs correction before saving. If the exact printing or price is missing, do not substitute another version or a zero value. We have not run the same physical cards through both apps, so these steps are a comparison method, not a test result.

The documented path after a scan

StepCardScanFoxLudex
ReviewConfirm a suggested catalog record, finish and languageIts scan guide says to verify card information and adjust the parallel
Price contextPublished prices and available history by raw condition or existing gradeThe guide shows an estimated price, last sold price and sales-over-time report
Next actionAdd a confirmed holding to a collectionAdd to collection or create an eBay listing

Both cover selected sports-card records and trading card games. CardScanFox has Pokémon, Magic, One Piece and Yu-Gi-Oh! catalog records. Check the exact printing and consult the football coverage guide before relying on a football match.

Choose based on selling plans

If you want to scan and publish an eBay listing, Ludex documents that handoff with eligible plans. CardScanFox currently offers an eBay search link for supported sports cards, not an in-app eBay listing tool. If you are sorting a stack into holdings and need raw copies and existing slabs valued separately, CardScanFox keeps those entries distinct in the portfolio.

Do not treat a listing ask as a sold price. Review actual transaction evidence before deciding what to charge.

How to compare the two fairly

Use the same known cards in both apps, including one base card, one parallel, and one graded slab. Record whether each result needs correction, how condition or grade is entered, and what happens after adding it to a collection. We have not run that controlled test, so this page does not claim a winner for recognition speed or accuracy.

Source: Ludex scan and price guide, reviewed November 24, 2026. Ludex plans and limits may change.

Compare scan workflow and plan limits

CardScanFox queues up to 10 separate photos in the mobile app and accepts one card per browser scan. Ludex documents one front image at a time in the phone app. Compare the exact TCG or sport before testing a large stack. The Ludex app lists Pokémon, Magic, VeeFriends and several sports. Its help page currently lists One Piece as unsupported in the scanner.

Ludex lists 200 identified scans per month and up to 60 portfolio cards on Free. Its monthly prices are $4.99 Lite, $9.99 Standard and $24.99 Pro. It lists 50 monthly eBay publications with Standard and 250 with Pro, with the Pro listing feature marked US only. Check the plan in your region.

CardScanFox vs Ludex questions.

How many free scans does CardScanFox include?

The iPhone app includes 10 successful free scans per account or guest identity, with no daily or monthly reset. The 10-image queue is the number of separate images you can review together. Check the current Premium offer in the app for its price and terms.

Is CardScanFox a Ludex alternative for organizing a stack?

Yes. CardScanFox queues up to 10 images for review and lets you add confirmed cards to a portfolio. Ludex also documents scanning and collection management; compare both on your own cards.

Can CardScanFox create an eBay listing like Ludex?

No. Ludex documents an eBay listing workflow. CardScanFox can provide an eBay search link for supported sports cards, but does not create an eBay listing.

Which scanner is more accurate?

We have not completed a controlled recognition test on the same cards in both apps, so we do not claim an accuracy winner.
